summary: An excerpt from a science-fiction novel set aboard the station Paraclete, where Ray and a companion choose Thai food at Bangkok House, run by Ng Uk-Thong. The passage describes the rats' favored status with the Thai franchisee, their late-night routine of queuing for broadcast array time, and the chaotic service of Uk-Thong's Brazilian wife, Maria Concita, who berates the kitchen staff in a hostile management style.
one_line: Ray and a companion pick Thai food at Bangkok House on Paraclete, where the rats' late-night broadcast routine and Maria Concita's abusive counter service are described.
key_facts: Ray and his companion agree after a heated discussion that they are both in the mood for Thai food.
Thai trash is always a rat favorite, for reasons Ray has never been able to fathom.
Ng Uk-Thong, the Thai franchisee on Paraclete, steadfastly refuses to strike a food-for-labor deal with the system vets.
The text suggests Uk-Thong is aware of his favored-nation status among the rat leadership.
Commander Sorensen does not let the rats use the broadcast array to multiply their fortunes until late in the evening.
The rats now rise late and assemble in a queue outside the Network Control hub just off the auxiliary communications bridge.
Bangkok House is nearly deserted when the rats arrive.
Ng Uk-Thong's Brazilian wife, Maria Concita, mans the service counter alone from a stool behind the cash register.
Maria Concita wears a floral print sarong and has a considerable bulk, described with comic exaggeration.
The chefs at Bangkok House generated very little raw waste because a good food processor covers a multitude of culinary sins.
Maria Concita's management style is described as legendary, hostile and howling toward the kitchen staff.
Maria Concita threatens the kitchen that Gucho will cut their throat with his box knife.
The rats' daytime habits include sending wives to theatres, shoving kids out onto the main concourse, and drinking themselves into stupors at their desks.
The narrator observes that a man's body should not become a personal metaphor system for a catalog of bad memories.
